core_obligations: Surjectivity of |U| -> |M|: C -> A integral (registered S7 integral-over-invariants lemma) and injective, cited Algebra lemma gives surjectivity.
For k algebraically closed: U(k) -> M(k) surjective - base change, nonzero integral extension over k, residue fields equal k.
R-invariance: a_0 = b t-sharp, a_1 = b s-sharp agree on C by definition of the invariants.

Converse for k-points: distinct maximal ideals m'_i != m of A (x)_C k (cited Algebra lemma) give f in m outside all m'_i; the norm g = Norm(t-sharp(f)) lies in the invariants C^1 of the base-change groupoid (registered determinant-trick lemma).

a_1(g) invertible (f nonzero at every point over a_1 of the artinian fibre) versus g non-invertible (f non-unit, t-sharp reflects units by faithful flatness, norm of a non-unit is a non-unit); the two flagged reference placeholders cover these elementary unit criteria.
Contradiction: the invariants-base-change sub-claims (2)(a),(2)(b) applied to C -> k show every element of C^1 is a unit or nilpotent.
Part (1): u_0, u_1 over the same m embed into k = k-bar(kappa(m)) as k-points; part (2) provides the connecting R-point; take its image.
proof_roadmap: integral-injective surjectivity chain + norm trick + contradiction via executed invariants sub-claims; placeholders are citation gaps only.
